instructions: Measure 2 cups of the corn into a sieve and run warm water over it for about 1 minute to thaw it. Shake it well and pat it dry with a clean towel. Thinly slice 1 of the green onions.

In a large bowl, mix the 1/3 cup flour, the 1/4 cup cornmeal, the egg, the green onion, the 1/8 tsp smoked paprika, the 1/2 tsp salt and the pinch of pepper. Stir in the corn and 1/2 cup of the Monterey Jack.
Add the 1/4 cup milk a little at a time, stirring as you go, until the mixture is moist but still holds together when you press it on a spoon. You may not need all of it.
Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium until it shimmers. Drop in 2 to 3 tbsp of the mixture per fritter, about 6 at a time, and flatten each one gently with a spatula.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the underside is golden and crisp. Flip them and cook the other side for 3 to 4 minutes. Move them to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and cook the rest of the mixture the same way.
Serve hot with 1/2 cup of the sour cream.
method_notes: Both make a batter of flour, egg and milk around plenty of corn kernels and cook spoonfuls until golden. Spend With Pennies (the lead) adds cornmeal, Monterey Jack, green onion and a little smoked paprika, shallow fries 2 to 3 tbsp portions in a couple of tablespoons of oil for 3 to 4 minutes a side and serves them with sour cream. Melissa's Southern Style Kitchen makes a sweeter, puffier batter with sugar and baking powder and deep fries it at 360°F. This follows the lead; its tablespoon of minced jalapeño is left out so the fritters stay mild.
